agree.reason: Dana gets her own $600K figure and a $75K cost against $125K–$300K in savings, and the IT concern is addressed head-on, so she would likely agree to a 20-minute call, though a cautious IT director might still balk.

honest.reason: Every number traces to the brief and 'more than half' is accurate (54%), but calling 2.2 'our smaller result' suggests a full range when only 3 of 6 customers track errors and one hasn't shared its numbers.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly turns price into $75K a year and both results into dollar savings against her own figure, which is conservative because hers is a floor, but it misses easier hooks like payback in months or roughly $15K cost per site against her returns cost per site.

right_comparison.reason: Doing nothing is implied as keeping $600K+ a year in returns, but the email never says outright what each month of waiting costs.

qualification.reason: Results vary widely between customers, but the email offers no checkable condition, such as a one-site pilot with a target mis-pick rate by a set date and what happens if it's missed.

objections.reason: The IT director's resistance is met with 'doesn't replace your WMS,' 'sits on top,' a three-week setup and an offer to walk IT through it first, and no objection is raised unnecessarily, though it could say more plainly that the WMS itself is untouched.

fit.reason: It is short, has a clear subject line, uses short paragraphs that read well on a phone and ends with a single ask.
